title: Example 18-7: Use of Freestanding Caret in an Exercise

illustrates.quote: Carets. Use a caret symbol when a caret (^) indicates an insertion is to be made. Follow print for spacing.

blocks.text: Insert an adjective where you see a ^.

resolution: Run A’s braille.lines is correct — confirmed directly against the source (line 14586 reads '": y see a @54' verbatim) and by forward-translating "Insert an adjective where you see a ^." through Emboss’s own translator (louis.translate, uebG2), which reproduces run A’s line character-for-character. Run B’s own '":]e y see a @54' does not occur anywhere in the source and does not forward-translate from any plausible English wording — a transcription error unique to run B (matches this task’s own advance "Known" note). Caret (^) is an ordinary UEB print symbol (not transcriber-defined, F-188 does not apply here) — confirmed live: translating a literal "^" character reproduces "@5" with zero Emboss-specific code, and the numbered exercise item "1. He has ^ hair. (long, shaggy, short)" forward-translates to the given braille’s second line exactly, parentheses included (ordinary UEB punctuation, ~F-187’s own contrast case).
